Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that starts a streaming recognizer with language and punctuation settings using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 2 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Option 3 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 4 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 5 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 6 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
import websockets
import json

class DeepgramStreamingRecognizer:
    def __init__(self, api_key: str, language: str = "en-US", punctuate: bool = True):
        self.api_key = api_key
        self.language = language
        self.punctuate = punctuate
        self.websocket_url = f"wss://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen?language={self.language}&punctuate={'true' if self.punctuate else 'false'}"
        self.transcript_queue = asyncio.Queue()

    async def _connect_and_transcribe(self, audio_generator):
        headers = {
            "Authorization": f"Token {self.api_key}"
        }
        async with websockets.connect(self.websocket_url, extra_headers=headers) as ws:
            async def send_audio():
                async for chunk in audio_generator:
                    if chunk:
                        await ws.send(chunk)
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "CloseStream"}))

            async def receive_transcriptions():
                async for message in ws:
                    response = json.loads(message)
                    if response.get("type") == "Results" and response["channel"]["alternatives"]:
                        transcript = response["channel"]["alternatives"][0]["transcript"]
                        if transcript:
                            await self.transcript_queue.put(transcript)
                    elif response.get("type") == "Error":
                        print(f"Deepgram Error: {response.get('message')}")
                        await self.transcript_queue.put(None) # Signal end or error
                        break

            await asyncio.gather(send_audio(), receive_transcriptions())

    async def start_recognition(self, audio_generator):
        """
        Starts the streaming speech recognition.

        Args:
            audio_generator: An async generator that yields audio chunks (bytes).
        Yields:
            Transcribed text segments as they become available.
        """
        await self._connect_and_transcribe(audio_generator)
        while not self.transcript_queue.empty():
            yield await self.transcript_queue.get()

async def dummy_audio_generator():
    """A dummy audio generator for demonstration purposes."""
    # In a real application, this would read from a microphone, file, etc.
    # For Deepgram, typically 16-bit PCM, 16000 Hz, mono
    print("Simulating audio input...")
    yield b'\x00' * 3200 # A small chunk of silent audio (16khz, 16bit, mono -> 2 bytes/sample * 1600 samples = 3200 bytes per 0.1s)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    # Deepgram expects raw audio, so we're just sending some bytes.
    # For a real test, you'd need actual audio data.
    yield b'\x01' * 6400 # Another chunk
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    print("Finished simulating audio.")
    yield None # Signal end of audio

async def main():
    api_key = os.getenv("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY")
    if not api_key:
        raise ValueError("DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable not set.")

    recognizer = DeepgramStreamingRecognizer(api_key=api_key, language="en-US", punctuate=True)

    print("Starting Deepgram streaming recognition...")
    async for transcript in recognizer.start_recognition(dummy_audio_generator()):
        if transcript:
            print(f"Transcript: {transcript}")
        else:
            print("Recognition ended or encountered an error.")
            break

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # To run this, you'll need a DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable set.
    # This example uses a dummy audio generator. For real usage, replace
    # `dummy_audio_generator` with an actual audio source.
    # For a quick test:
    # 1. Set DEEPGRAM_API_KEY="YOUR_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY"
    # 2. python your_script_name.py
    # You won't get meaningful transcription from the dummy generator,
    # but it will demonstrate the connection and basic flow.
    # To hear an error about invalid audio, uncomment the next line
    # or ensure you're sending valid audio data.
    # asyncio.run(main()) # Uncomment to run, but will only send silent/random bytes
    print("To run this example, uncomment `asyncio.run(main())` and set the DEEPGRAM_API_KEY environment variable.")
    print("Note: The `dummy_audio_generator` sends silent/random bytes, so no meaningful transcription will occur.")
    print("It demonstrates the setup and streaming loop.")
